subject: Physics
schema_note: Keyed by topic_id (matches physics_syllabus_jee_main.json). Same field set as the JEE Advanced NCERT-context file, with 'hard_archetypes' recalibrated to JEE-Main-level difficulty (single/dual-concept, not the multi-topic fusion typical of Advanced) and 'banned_easy_templates' generally left as a note that direct-substitution questions are wanted, not excluded, since that is the opposite convention from the Advanced file.

concepts: Propagation of error in a derived quantity
formulas: Δz/z = Δx/x + Δy/y for z = xy or x/y
methods: Identify whether the target quantity is a product/quotient (add % errors) or a sum/difference (add absolute errors) before combining
traps: Adding absolute errors for a product/quotient relation instead of percentage errors
hard_archetypes: Two- or three-quantity error propagation through a power-law formula (e.g. finding max % error in g = 4π²L/T²)
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Statistical/regression treatment of data; least-squares fitting

concepts: Equations of motion under constant acceleration
formulas: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as
methods: Resolve projectile motion into independent horizontal and vertical components before combining
traps: Confusing average speed with the magnitude of average velocity
Sign errors when taking 'up' as positive vs 'down' as positive
hard_archetypes: River-boat/rain-man relative-velocity problems requiring a vector diagram
Projectile launched from a height, asked for range on a lower/inclined surface
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Projectile motion in polar or non-Cartesian coordinates as a formal topic

methods: Draw a free-body diagram for each block separately before writing Newton's-second-law equations
Check whether the applied force exceeds limiting static friction before assuming motion occurs
traps: Assuming friction is always at its maximum (kinetic) value without checking whether slipping actually occurs
hard_archetypes: Two-block system connected over a pulley with friction on an incline
A block on a wedge that itself is free to slide on a frictionless floor
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Pseudo-force analysis in a formally non-inertial, non-uniformly accelerating frame beyond a simple lift/wedge scenario

methods: Use the work-energy theorem directly instead of full kinematics when the force varies with position
traps: Applying the 1D elastic-collision formula directly to a 2D oblique collision
Assuming kinetic energy is conserved in an inelastic collision (only momentum is)
hard_archetypes: A block sliding down a track of varying height/friction, found using energy conservation plus a collision at the bottom
Oblique 2D collision requiring component-wise momentum conservation
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Relativistic energy-momentum relations

formulas: a = g sinθ / (1 + I/mR²) for rolling down an incline
methods: Apply angular momentum conservation about a fixed axis whenever the net external torque about that axis is zero
traps: Using τ = Iα about a non-fixed axis without justification
Forgetting that static (not kinetic) friction usually provides the torque for rolling without slipping
hard_archetypes: A ring/disc/sphere released on a rough incline, asked for the condition for pure rolling
Angular momentum conservation when a person on a rotating disc pulls their arms in
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Gyroscopic precession

methods: Use energy conservation (KE + PE) for problems that move a mass between two radii rather than force equations alone
traps: Forgetting gravitational PE is negative (taken as zero at infinity)
Confusing orbital velocity with escape velocity by a factor of √2
hard_archetypes: Finding the extra velocity needed to escape from a circular orbit
Energy required to move a satellite from one orbital radius to another
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Gravitational field of a non-uniform or partially removed mass distribution (this stays in JEE Advanced territory)

concepts: Excess pressure across a curved surface
Equation of continuity and Bernoulli's theorem
formulas: Excess pressure in a drop: 2T/r; in a bubble: 4T/r
methods: Apply the equation of continuity (A1v1 = A2v2) before applying Bernoulli's theorem in a flow problem
traps: Forgetting buoyant-force correction (ρ-σ) when applying Stokes' law
Mixing up the factor of 2 vs 4 between a liquid drop and a soap bubble
hard_archetypes: Efflux speed from a hole in a tank combined with range/time-of-flight of the emerging jet
A sphere falling through a viscous fluid, asked to find terminal velocity or time to reach it
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Reynolds number and turbulence criteria (removed from the 2025-26 syllabus)

concepts: Cv, Cp and the relation Cp - Cv = R
methods: Identify the process type (isothermal/adiabatic/isochoric/isobaric) first — it fixes which work-done formula applies
traps: Using the isothermal work formula for an adiabatic process or vice versa
Sign errors on ΔQ, ΔW convention (work done BY the gas vs ON the gas)
hard_archetypes: A cyclic process on a P-V diagram, asked for net work done or efficiency of the cycle
Mixed isothermal + adiabatic multi-step process, asked for final state variables
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Carnot-engine efficiency derivation as a standalone examinable item (removed from the 2025-26 syllabus, though the underlying second-law idea can still appear qualitatively)

concepts: Kinetic interpretation of pressure and temperature
Degrees of freedom and equipartition of energy
rms, average and most probable speed
formulas: Internal energy of an ideal gas: U = (f/2)nRT
methods: Identify the gas's degrees of freedom (monatomic f=3, diatomic f=5) before computing Cv, Cp or internal energy
traps: Using f=3 for a diatomic gas (forgetting rotational degrees of freedom)
Confusing v_rms, v_avg and v_mp (they differ by known numeric factors, not equal)
hard_archetypes: Mixture of two different gases in a container, asked for the common rms speed or pressure
A gas undergoing a process where degrees-of-freedom-based Cv must be combined with the first law
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Maxwell-Boltzmann speed-distribution derivation (only qualitative shape is expected)

methods: Identify the restoring-force law (F ∝ -x) to confirm SHM before applying the standard SHM formulas
traps: Confusing angular frequency ω with ordinary frequency f (factor of 2π)
Sign errors when writing displacement vs acceleration phase relationship
hard_archetypes: Combining two SHMs of the same frequency along the same line, asked for resultant amplitude/phase
Vibrating air-column problem (open/closed pipe) combined with a beats calculation
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Forced/damped oscillations and mechanical resonance as a formal derivation; Doppler effect in sound (both removed from the 2025-26 syllabus)

concepts: Gauss's law for symmetric charge distributions
Electric dipole in a uniform field
formulas: Torque on dipole τ = pE sinθ
methods: Choose a Gaussian surface that matches the symmetry of the charge distribution before applying Gauss's law
traps: Sign errors in potential when charges of both signs are present
Forgetting that inserting a dielectric increases capacitance but a battery being connected/disconnected changes what stays constant (Q or V)
hard_archetypes: A parallel-plate capacitor with a dielectric slab partially inserted, asked for the resulting capacitance
Network of capacitors in a bridge-like arrangement, asked for equivalent capacitance or charge distribution
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Van de Graaff generator design details; energy density derivation beyond the standard formula

formulas: Potentiometer: emf ratio = length ratio (balance points)
methods: Assign loop currents and apply KVL/KCL systematically for multi-loop circuits rather than guessing current directions
traps: Sign errors when traversing a loop against the assumed current direction
Mixing up internal resistance's effect on terminal voltage during charging vs discharging
hard_archetypes: Multi-loop resistor network requiring simultaneous KVL/KCL equations
Meter-bridge or potentiometer problem combined with an unknown internal resistance or end-correction
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Non-linear circuit elements beyond a simple diode; AC circuit analysis (that belongs to M14)

M13.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
concepts: Force on a charge/current in a magnetic field
methods: Superpose the fields of multiple current segments using Biot-Savart before combining magnitudes/directions with the right-hand rule
traps: Sign/direction errors from the right-hand rule in cross products
Forgetting the velocity component parallel to B is unaffected by the magnetic force
hard_archetypes: Magnetic field at a point due to a combination of straight-wire segments and an arc
Converting a galvanometer to a given-range ammeter or voltmeter, finding the shunt/series resistance
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Helical/cycloidal motion in combined non-uniform E and B fields (JEE-Advanced-level fusion)

methods: Use Lenz's law direction reasoning before computing the magnitude of an induced EMF
traps: Sign errors in Lenz's law direction (the induced effect opposes the change in flux, not the field itself)
Confusing peak and rms values when computing AC power
hard_archetypes: A rod sliding on rails in a magnetic field with a resistor/capacitor in the circuit, finding induced current as a function of time
Series LCR circuit problem requiring both the resonance condition and the power factor
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Three-phase AC systems; detailed transformer loss analysis

concepts: Mutual perpendicularity of E, B and propagation direction
methods: Cross-reference a given frequency/wavelength with the standard EM-spectrum band ranges for identification questions
traps: Confusing which of E0 or B0 is numerically larger in SI units
Mixing up the frequency ranges of adjacent EM-spectrum bands
hard_archetypes: Given an expression for E(x,t) or B(x,t), deduce the other field and the direction of propagation
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Maxwell's equations in full differential form; radiation-pressure numericals combined with intensity (Advanced-level fusion)

concepts: YDSE fringe width; single-slit diffraction minima
methods: Treat each optical element sequentially in a multi-element system: the image of one becomes the object for the next
Keep the sign convention consistent across the whole problem, especially with virtual images
traps: Sign-convention slips between mirror and lens formulas
Using double-slit interference formulas for a single-slit diffraction question or vice versa
hard_archetypes: A two-lens (or lens+mirror) combination requiring sequential image tracing
YDSE with a thin dielectric slab inserted in one slit, asked for the resulting fringe shift
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Diffraction-grating resolving-power formalism; chromatic/spherical aberration beyond a qualitative mention

M17.chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
methods: Use the stopping-potential vs frequency graph (slope = h/e, intercept related to φ) to extract work function or threshold frequency
traps: Forgetting the work function φ differs by material
Mixing up photon energy (hf) with the electron's kinetic energy after emission
hard_archetypes: Given stopping potentials at two different frequencies, find Planck's constant and the work function simultaneously
Photoelectric effect combined with de Broglie wavelength of the emitted electron
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Compton effect derivation in full detail

concepts: Bohr model energy levels and transitions
formulas: N = N0 e^{-λt}; activity A = λN
methods: Use an energy-level diagram to identify which transition matches a given photon energy or wavelength
traps: Confusing half-life with mean life (factor of ln2)
Forgetting mass number/atomic number bookkeeping in alpha/beta decay
hard_archetypes: Given the activity of a sample at two different times, find the decay constant and initial number of atoms
A hydrogen-like ion (Z>1) transition problem requiring the Z² scaling of Bohr energy levels
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Sequential parent-daughter-granddaughter decay chains with simultaneous differential equations (this stays Advanced-level)

formulas: Diode equation qualitatively: forward bias -> low resistance, reverse bias -> high resistance (up to breakdown)
methods: Read the I-V characteristic graph directly to classify forward/reverse bias and identify breakdown (Zener) region
traps: Mixing up which diode terminal is forward-biased in a given circuit diagram
Confusing the truth tables of NAND and NOR, or of OR and NOR
hard_archetypes: A circuit combining a Zener diode as a voltage regulator, asked for load/series-resistor current
A combinational logic circuit (2-3 gates) requiring the final truth table or Boolean output
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Unlike JEE Advanced, JEE Main deliberately tests many direct, single-formula substitution questions — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Transistor amplifier/oscillator circuit analysis (removed from the 2025-26 syllabus); integrated-circuit design

concepts: Least count and reading a vernier/screw-gauge scale
Reading standard experiment graphs (u-v, I-V, resonance)
Identifying an experimental setup from a diagram
formulas: Least count (vernier) = 1 main-scale division − 1 vernier-scale division
Least count (screw gauge) = pitch / number of circular-scale divisions
methods: Match the described apparatus/graph shape to the specific NCERT experiment it belongs to before answering
traps: Ignoring zero error when reading a vernier caliper or screw gauge
Confusing which quantity is plotted on which axis for a given experiment's standard graph
hard_archetypes: Given a set of raw vernier/screw-gauge readings including zero error, compute the corrected measurement
Identify a device (diode/Zener/LED) purely from its I-V characteristic curve shape
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'name this apparatus' recall question with no reading/calculation is acceptable and common for this unit — do not exclude it (unlike other JEE Main units, pure recall is a legitimate archetype here).
out_of_scope: Any experiment not among the 18 standard NCERT-listed experiments for this unit
